sources.retrievalStatus: Official HTML returned HTTP 403; a browser PDF print was captured manually

steps: Subtract eligible Social Security, Medicare, Massachusetts, United States, or railroad retirement deductions until the annual $2,000 cap is reached.
Subtract the frequency-specific exemption factor unless zero exemptions are claimed.
Annualize the result using the actual number of payroll periods, including 26 or 27 for biweekly payroll.
Apply 5% through $1,107,750 and 9% above that threshold.
Divide annual tax by payroll periods, subtract head-of-household and blindness tax values, and add requested periodic withholding.

supplementalWages.aggregation: Combine adjusted supplemental payment, prior supplemental payments from the payer in the year, and annualized regular wages from that payer.
supplementalWages.aboveThreshold: Withhold the lesser of 9% of adjusted supplemental wages, or 9% of the aggregate excess over the threshold plus 5% of the remainder.

residencyAndWorkRules.residentRule: Withhold from all Massachusetts resident wages for services inside or outside Massachusetts.
residencyAndWorkRules.nonresidentRule: Withhold only on Massachusetts-source wages for services performed in Massachusetts.
residencyAndWorkRules.allocation: Use exact Massachusetts pay when determinable; otherwise multiply gross income by Massachusetts workdays divided by total workdays.
residencyAndWorkRules.partialDay: Treat as a Massachusetts workday unless the employee proves more than half the day was worked outside Massachusetts.

frequencies.due: 15th after month, except quarter-end months due last day after month
Within three business days after days 7, 15, 22, and month end; quarterly return remains required
